kept.title: How many donors are needed to see donor-level predictability? Detectability thresholds for leave-one-donor-out ridge R^2 against a leave-one-out-mean benchmark, and in-sample versus out-of-sample power, under a hierarchical (spots in donors) design
kept.core_claim: The round-9 finding that donor-level prediction does not beat a constant for the median Visium gene can mean two different things: no population signal, or signal below the detectability threshold of a K-donor LODO R^2 with a p>>K embedding. Claim: for ridge heads on donor-mean embeddings the expected LODO R^2 against the LOO-training-mean benchmark has a closed form in K, the spectrum of the donor-mean embedding covariance, the penalty and the signal alignment, with an explicit break-even population R^2 threshold that is a function of that spectrum (not just n and p), and a companion in-sample (permutation) test that can detect predictability the LODO statistic cannot.
kept.formal_result_sketch: Setup: donor means x_d in R^p, scalar donor-level target y_d = x_d' beta + a_d + e_d (a_d unforecastable donor shift, shared across genes), K donors, ridge with penalty lambda, LODO with training-mean benchmark. (1) Exact finite-K expression for E[R2_oos] via leave-one-out hat-matrix identities: E[R2_oos] = 1 - E[sum_d (e_d^LODO)^2]/E[sum_d (y_d - ybar_{-d})^2], where the denominator carries the factor K/(K-1) (the LOO-mean benchmark is negatively correlated with the held-out label) and the numerator depends on the leverage distribution h_dd(lambda) (Tipton's design-efficiency idea) and on the signal's projection onto the ridge-shrunk eigendirections. (2) Theorem: break-even rho*(K, spectrum, lambda) such that E[R2_oos]>0 iff rho^2 > rho*; in the proportional regime p/K -> gamma with isotropic spectrum rho* -> a deterministic function of gamma and lambda; with a decaying spectrum (as real embeddings have) rho* is governed by an effective rank. (3) Power comparison: for a permutation test on the in-sample ridge fit versus on the LODO R^2, a local-alternative analysis (Inoue-Kilian analogue, exchangeable donors rather than time series) giving an explicit power ordering. Assumed: exchangeable donors, Gaussian-or-sub-Gaussian donor means, fixed or CV-chosen lambda (the CV-chosen case is the hard part and is the risk). Not claimed: any statement across genes (the cross-gene dependence via the shared factor is the excluded FCP territory).
kept.data_test: Predict before running: for CCRCC (24 donors), INDIANA_KIDNEY (25) and LUNG_XENIUM (15), compute the donor-mean embedding spectrum for hoptimus0, uni_v2, resnet50, evaluate rho*(K, spectrum, lambda) and compare with the observed per-gene LODO R^2 in results/round9 (the median Visium gene should sit below rho*; lung alveolar markers CA4/AGER/SFTPC at R^2 near 0.9 far above). Then run the in-sample permutation statistic per gene and report the number of genes that are in-sample detectable but LODO-negative. Toy check done in this session (provisional, 150 replicates per cell): K=24, p=500 isotropic Gaussian embedding, ridge penalty = p, unit noise; population R^2 = 0.4 gave mean LODO R^2 = +0.012, P(LODO R^2>0) = 0.60, permutation-test power 0.127 (in-sample ridge statistic) and 0.14 (LODO statistic); at R^2 = 0 the LODO R^2 averaged -0.013 and P(>0) = 0.46. So a large population R^2 can be invisible at K=24, but this toy did not show an in-sample power advantage, so the Inoue-Kilian-type ordering in claim (3) is not supported by this run and may fail.
kept.second_application: ACS PUMS 2018: units are the 51 states/DC (or ~2,400 PUMAs); predict state-level mean outcomes (income, commute time) from aggregated covariate embeddings, and test whether the threshold predicts which outcomes beat the leave-one-state-out mean.
kept.finance_transfer: Direct: Goyal-Welch / Campbell-Thompson equity-premium predictability with a short monthly or annual sample and many predictors; the same threshold and in-sample vs OOS power logic apply to predictive regressions with few periods; also K markets or K periods in panel forecasting.
kept.closest_prior_work: Tipton arXiv:2610.18781 (expected LOO R^2 for OLS and ridge, break-even threshold, leverage-based design efficiency; no clustering; read: abstract, scope, limitations); Hawinkel-Waegeman-Maere 2023 (unbiased OOS R^2 and SE, iid); Economics Letters 2026 on finite-sample Campbell-Thompson R^2 bias; Inoue-Kilian 2005 (in- vs out-of-sample power, time series, fixed p); Campbell-Thompson 2008.
kept.what_is_open: (a) The hierarchical version: spots nested in donors with a donor-level estimand, where the threshold depends on the donor-mean embedding spectrum rather than the spot-level one. (b) The p>>K non-isotropic-spectrum case with CV-chosen penalty (Tipton fixes the penalty). (c) An exchangeable-units analogue of Inoue-Kilian power ordering for ridge/permutation tests (my toy did not show the ordering). (d) The sampling distribution of LODO R^2, which Tipton leaves open (the break-even design wins only about half the time). Nothing here is a new principle; a reviewer would call (a)-(b) an extension of Tipton 2026.
kept.risks: The core threshold is already published (Tipton, Oct 2026) and the bias of OOS R^2 against a mean benchmark is classical; the remainder is a clustered/high-dimensional extension that may read as incremental. The toy run did not support an in-sample power advantage. Tipton's paper was read only in part (abstract, scope, limitations, not the proofs). Potentially overlaps the BENCH item if framed as comparing encoders.

kept.title: Two-scale identification of the histology-predictability ceiling: scale-free encoder efficiency and skilful-scale inference on re-aggregated Xenium data
kept.core_claim: On Xenium, spots can be re-aggregated to any block size A. If unit-level noise (count noise plus cell-to-cell variability) is independent across units given a latent field mu, then Var(block mean) = S(A) + tau^2/A, so a two-scale estimator in the spirit of two-scale realized variance identifies tau^2 and S(A) without a Poisson model or thinning, giving a ceiling R2_max(A) = S(A)/(S(A)+tau^2/A) and a scale-free efficiency eta_k(A) = R2_k(A)/R2_max(A) for each encoder k. The ratio of two encoders' correlations is noise-free (the common attenuation cancels), so encoder rankings can be compared across scales, and a skilful scale A*_k = min{A: eta_k(A) >= c} gets a donor-level interval.
kept.formal_result_sketch: Assume (A1) y_i = mu(s_i) + eta_i with eta_i independent given mu, E[eta_i|mu]=0, Var = tau^2 (or tau^2(s_i) known up to a smooth function); (A2) predictors f_k are measurable functions of the image and independent of eta given mu; (A3) mu is second-order stationary within donor with finite range. Results sought: (i) identity r_k(A) = rho_k(A) * sqrt(Rel(A)) with Rel(A)=S(A)/(S(A)+tau^2/A) common to all k, hence r_1/r_2 = rho_1/rho_2 invariant to outcome noise; (ii) consistency and an explicit variance of the two-scale estimator of tau^2 when neighbouring units are spatially correlated in mu (the analogue of dependent-noise TSRV, with the range of mu in the role of the noise dependence); (iii) a sign-flip/t_{K-1} interval across K donors for eta_1(A)-eta_2(A) and for A*_k, valid under exchangeable donors; (iv) a design result: the scale A_opt maximising power to separate two encoders trades the noise reduction (rises with A) against the number of independent blocks (falls with A), giving a closed form under an exponential covariance for mu. Pieces (ii) and (iv) are the places where something new might exist; (i) is nearly an identity.
kept.data_test: LUNG_XENIUM (15 donors, 343 genes): aggregate cells into blocks of increasing size, estimate tau^2 and S(A) by the two-scale estimator, and validate against an independent Poisson-thinning ceiling computed from raw counts. Predictions written before the run: ceiling follows A/(A+c) shape, encoder efficiency eta_k(A) is flat or slowly rising in A for composition-marker genes and rises toward 1 only at coarse A for the rest, and encoder ranking by correlation ratio is stable across A. Visium tasks cannot be re-aggregated, so only a coarsening-by-neighbour check is possible there.
kept.second_application: ACS PUMS 2018: person-level outcomes (log wage, commute) aggregated to PUMA, then state; the replicate weights give an independent estimate of the sampling-noise variance to validate the two-scale estimate and the ceiling as a function of aggregation size.
kept.finance_transfer: Very direct: realized variance, microstructure noise and signature plots; two-scale and multi-scale estimators; robust-loss and proxy-based forecast comparison (Patton, Hansen-Lunde); multi-horizon forecast comparison (Quaedvlieg) with horizon replaced by aggregation scale.
kept.closest_prior_work: Zhang-Mykland-Ait-Sahalia 2005 and Ait-Sahalia-Mykland-Zhang 2011 (two-scale realized variance; read as search excerpts, not the full PDF, which the sandbox blocked); Bellehumeur 1997 and geostatistical change of support (nugget); Spearman-Brown/generalizability theory (reliability of aggregated units); Mittermaier-Roberts 2010 skilful spatial scale; Quaedvlieg multi-horizon SPA; the project's own THIN item (noise ceiling via thinning, graded mostly_taken).
kept.what_is_open: Narrow: (a) a thinning-free identification of the unpredictable-by-image floor from scale dependence with spatially dependent signal, with a stated variance; (b) the donor-level exchangeable inference for scale curves and skilful scales; (c) the power-optimal evaluation scale for separating encoders; (d) the first application to HEST-style histology-to-expression data (empirical ablations exist, no theory found). Each component has a close precedent in another field.
kept.risks: Each ingredient exists in finance, geostatistics, psychometrics or weather verification, and THIN covers the noise-ceiling application; the formal remainder (ii) and (iv) may collapse to textbook variance algebra. The assumption that unit-level noise is independent of the image-derived prediction is false if cell composition within a block drives both, and the ceiling would then be overstated. Only Xenium supports re-aggregation, so the empirical test rests on one task with 15 donors. Overlaps SpatialLens 'change of support' items in the digest.

kept.title: Donor-count asymptotics for pooled ridge probes: effective sample size G, non-separable donor offsets, and a donor-level risk estimator
kept.core_claim: For frozen-embedding ridge probes trained on spots pooled over G donors with n_d->infinity spots each, the new-donor risk is governed by G (not by total spots n) and by the spectrum of the donor-offset covariance. Pooled (uncentred) second-moment matrix is Sigma_W + (1/G) sum_d mu_d mu_d^T, i.e. a fixed matrix plus a Wishart-type term with aspect ratio p/G, and the donor label offsets a_d (depth factor, invisible to histology) enter the normal equations as noise along the donor-offset directions. Claim: (i) risk has a G-driven interpolation peak near G ~ effective rank of Sigma_B that is invariant to n_d, so adding spots cannot fix it; (ii) within-donor (fixed-effects) training removes the term and its risk decays like p/(G n_d); (iii) a donor-level leave-one-donor-out shortcut is consistent for the new-donor risk in this regime even though the label-offset correlation differs from the feature-offset correlation (the case CorrGCV excludes).
kept.formal_result_sketch: Model: x_di = mu_d + w_di, mu_d ~ (0, Sigma_B), w ~ (0, Sigma_W); y_di = beta_d^T w_di + gamma^T mu_d + a_d + eps_di, a_d ~ (0, tau^2) independent of mu_d. Regime: n_d -> infinity, then p, G -> infinity with p/G -> gamma, Sigma_B and Sigma_W general with bounded spectra (no proportionality). Assumed: Gaussian (or Gaussian-universality) mu_d, bounded spectra, beta_d random effects with covariance Omega. Aimed theorems: T1, almost-sure limit of the new-donor within-donor excess risk of pooled ridge as a fixed-point equation obtained by free additive convolution of Sigma_W with the Marchenko-Pastur-type law of (1/G) M M^T (M = [mu_1..mu_G]); T2, the limit has a non-monotone G-profile with a peak at gamma ~ 1 (ridgeless) and a persistent floor tau^2 * tr(Sigma_B Sigma_lambda^-2 Sigma_W)/G for tuned lambda; T3, fixed-effects ridge limit p/(G n_d)-type; T4, a donor-block Woodbury leave-one-donor-out estimator (exact) and its almost-sure consistency for the T1 limit, plus a failure statement for iid GCV and for CorrGCV when noise and data correlations differ. Lower-bound corollary: between-donor detection floor from Verzelen-Gassiat applied to donor means (n:=G) is stated as a corollary, not a claim of novelty.
kept.data_test: No new data pull, but needs Longleaf embeddings (not run here). (1) On CCRCC (24 donors), INDIANA_KIDNEY (25), LUNG_XENIUM (15 donors, many spots each, closest to the n_d->inf regime), for hoptimus0, resnet50, uni_v2: LODO within-donor correlation of pooled-uncentred vs donor-centred ridge heads. (2) Subsample donors (G=6..max) and spots per donor (10^2..10^4 on Xenium): theory predicts no gain from more spots per donor for the pooled head once n_d is large, and a G-profile with a peak. (3) Estimate the spectrum of the between-donor covariance of donor-mean embeddings per encoder to evaluate the T1 formula and compare with realised LODO risk; compare the donor-level LODO shortcut with brute-force LODO. Predictions to be written before the run. Toy simulation done here (p=100, Gaussian, s=2, tau=2, 20-30 reps; PROVISIONAL, synthetic only): pooled-uncentred ridge excess coefficient error at oracle lambda was 0.35 (G=24), 0.56 (G=48), 0.78 (G=96, n_d=3000) versus ||beta||^2=0.5, with no improvement from n_d=300 to 3000, while within-centred ridge error fell from 0.014 to 0.0014 with n_d; this supports a G-driven, n_d-invariant failure but also shows the effect is the fixed-effects phenomenon.

kept.title: Depth-equivariant evaluation of count predictors under an unobserved multiplicative donor factor: exact log1p loadings, per-gene between-donor ceilings, and a scale-profiled ranking criterion
kept.core_claim: If counts are Poisson(s_d * lambda) with a donor-level scale s_d that the image cannot see, then (i) on the log1p scale the depth factor loads on gene g with an exact, gene-specific weight e(s*lambda_g) that rises from 0 to 1 with the mean count, so the shared PC1, the partial removal by library-size normalisation, and the between-donor R^2 ceiling are all predictable from mean counts; (ii) the usual criteria (log1p MSE, raw Poisson deviance, donor-level R^2) rank predictors by the realised donor-depth mix, whereas the scale-profiled (conditional-on-donor-total, multinomial) deviance ranks them by the shape component only and is noise-robust in Patton's sense.
kept.formal_result_sketch: Setup: y_ig | lambda_ig, s_d ~ Poisson(s_d*lambda_ig) (extension: mixed Poisson with Fano factor >= 1), s_d independent of images; predictor depends on images only. Prop 1 (exact loading): with h(m)=E log1p(Poisson(m)), the Poisson derivative identity gives h'(m)=E[log((Y+2)/(Y+1))], hence dE[l]/dlog s = e(m):=m*h'(m), strictly increasing from 0 to 1. Corollaries: first-order loading of the donor-level depth factor on gene g is e(m_g); first-order between-donor R^2 ceiling is 1 - e_g^2 Var(log s)/Var_between(l_g) with delta-method remainder bound to be proved. Prop 2 (ranking): ordering of two predictors under log1p-MSE and raw Poisson deviance is a functional of the law of s_d (counterexample below); the scale-profiled loss min_a L(a*p, y) with a=sum y / sum p is invariant to s_d. Conjecture/target theorem 3: among Bregman losses, profiling gives an s_d-invariant ranking that coincides with the ranking under the latent lambda iff phi(x)=x log x up to affine terms (a Patton necessary-and-sufficient analogue with homogeneity of degree 0, QLIKE-like). Verified only numerically so far: the identity (finite-difference vs exact Poisson sums agree to 6 digits; e(m)=0.034, 0.184, 0.474, 0.799, 0.948, 0.983 at m=0.05, 0.3, 1, 3, 10, 30) and a toy ranking flip (N=20000 cells, one seed): predictor with small shape error but half-level beats a level-correct noisier predictor at s<=1 under log1p-MSE and raw deviance but loses at s>=2, while the profiled deviance prefers the first predictor at every s in {0.25,0.5,1,2,4}.

kept.title: What block-scale count data identify about cell-scale predictive skill: support-variation identification, sharp identified sets and a finance-style signature plot
kept.core_claim: A Visium spot pools m_j cells (nuclei counts are observed per spot) while Xenium resolves single cells. Under within-spot second-order exchangeability and Poisson-or-worse counting noise, the spot-level variance of counts and the spot-level covariance with predictions are quadratic in m (variance-ratio structure), so cell-scale variance components and cell-scale skill are point identified when m varies exogenously, and set identified (sharp interval) when it does not. The interval is c0 in [C - (m-1)*sqrt(kappa_p*kappa_lambda), C + (m-1)*sqrt(kappa_p*kappa_lambda)] intersected with the Cauchy-Schwarz box, where C is the per-cell block cross-covariance and kappa are between-cell covariances; shape restrictions (cross-covariance non-increasing in distance) shrink it. Gap in the same spirit explains why a 55-um spot cannot reveal cell-scale skill, and gives a testable scale-extrapolation law.
kept.formal_result_sketch: Model: cell i in spot j has latent intensity Lambda_i, prediction component P_i; within-spot compound symmetry with cell-level moments (mu, tau^2, v_p, c0) and between-cell covariances (kappa_lambda, kappa_p, c1); counts Y_j | Lambda ~ Poisson(sum Lambda_i) (or Fano >= 1). Then Var(Y|m)=m*mu + m*tau^2 + m(m-1)*kappa_lambda, Cov(P,Y|m)=m*c0 + m(m-1)*c1, Var(P|m)=m*v_p + m(m-1)*kappa_p. Theorem 1: if m is independent of (Lambda,P) within strata and takes >=3 distinct values, (c0, c1, kappa, tau^2) are identified and the Poisson-corrected cell-scale skill rho0=c0/sqrt(v_p*tau_tot^2) follows. Theorem 2 (single support m): sharp identified set as above from PSD of the 2x2 between-cell block (|c1| <= sqrt(kappa_p*kappa_lambda)); it is wide when kappa is large, which is the formal version of the ecological non-identification. Theorem 3 (shape-restricted): with a nonincreasing cross-covariance in distance and several supports (single spots, unions of neighbouring spots), sharp bounds by a linear program in the style of Moon's partial-identification programs; plus a CLT for the estimated polynomial coefficients with spatially mixing blocks. Not yet derived in full or simulated; the single-support interval was derived by hand and the PSD step is the only inequality used.
kept.data_test: LUNG_XENIUM (cell-level truth): coarsen pseudo-spots by pooling neighbouring ones (predictions averaged over neighbouring patch embeddings), fit the quadratic-in-m curves on supports >= 2 pseudo-spots, extrapolate to the 55-um pseudo-spot and check coverage of the identified set. Caveat: embeddings exist only at pseudo-spot level, so only coarsening is possible without new GPU embedding of sub-patches; finer-than-spot predictions are not available. Visium tasks (CCRCC, INDIANA_KIDNEY): use nuclei count per spot as support instrument, with a sensitivity parameter for non-exogenous cell density. kept.title: Predictable rank under a pervasive group-level nuisance: within/between reduced-rank selection when groups are fewer than features
kept.core_claim: Model: y_i = B^T x_i + f_g(i) lambda + e_i for spot i in donor g, B (p x m) of rank r (the histology-predictable gene programmes), f_g lambda a rank-1 donor-level nuisance (the depth/detection factor, PC1 share 0.650 on CCRCC, 0.343 on LUNG_XENIUM), and x_i = x_i^w + mu_g with donor-level embedding shifts mu_g spanning G-1 < p directions. Claim: (i) rank rules applied to pooled data over-select by the nuisance rank, because donor-level covariate variation can reproduce any donor-level response vector; (ii) pooled leave-donor-out CV rank selection under-selects (here: returns 0) because the pooled coefficient absorbs the between-donor component and pollutes held-out-donor predictions; (iii) a two-level pair (r_within, r_between) with r_between <= G-1 is identified, r_within is consistently estimated after donor demeaning, and r_between is tested exactly by donor-level sign-flips. The number a practitioner reports as "how many gene programmes does histology predict" is therefore not r unless the level is stated.
kept.formal_result_sketch: Assumptions: iid-Gaussian (later sub-Gaussian) within-donor errors, G fixed, n_g -> infinity, p/n_g fixed or p fixed, nuisance rank k0 with eigenvalue above the Bunea-She-Wegkamp / Bing-Wegkamp threshold lambda > 2(sqrt(m)+sqrt(q))^2 sigma^2. Prop 1 (overshoot, SNR-conditional): if the donor-shift matrix M (G x p) has rank G-1 and its signal-to-noise exceeds the within-donor design noise, the pooled projection captures the group indicator span up to o_p(1) angle, so P(r_hat_pooled = r + k0) -> 1. This needs a sin-theta argument that I have only sketched; the toy run supports it but does not prove it. Prop 2 (within consistency): donor demeaning removes both mu_g and f_g lambda exactly, so the problem is iid-row RRR with n-G residual df and Bing-Wegkamp Thm 8-type consistency applies (this part is a reduction to a known theorem). Prop 4 (pooled leave-donor-out CV failure): lower bound on its excess error in terms of ||B_between||^2 and the donor-shift covariance. kept.title: Empirical Bayes for gene-wise predictive skill under donor-shared estimation error: non-concentration of the estimated prior and an effective number of independent genes
kept.core_claim: Estimates theta_hat_g (Fisher-z of the within-donor correlation, or leave-donor-out R2) satisfy theta_hat_g = theta_g + lambda_g^T F + u_g, where F is the realised draw of a few donor- and spot-level factors shared by all genes (same test donors, same spot-level depth). Claim: the NPMLE of the prior of true skill converges, as the number of genes J grows with the number of donors G fixed, to the true prior convolved with the realised common shift lambda-bar^T F, not to the true prior. Posterior means and functionals (fraction of genes with skill above c) therefore keep an O_p(1) error that depends on G and the factor loadings, not on J; the effective number of independent genes is J/(1+(J-1) rho-bar).
kept.formal_result_sketch: Assume (theta_g, lambda_g) iid from a joint law, u_g independent N(0, s_g^2), F ~ N(0, Sigma_F/G) (donor-level factor with G effective df). Prop 1: conditional on F, the marginal density of theta_hat is g* convolved with N(lambda^T F, s^2) mixed over lambda; NPMLE converges (Kiefer-Wolfowitz, Soloff et al. type bounds) to that conditional mixture, so functional error converges to a nonzero constant |lambda-bar^T F| in the location and variance-inflated components as J -> infinity. Prop 2 (lower bound): any estimator not using a null atom, negative-control genes or other identification of lambda-bar^T F has minimax risk for the fraction functional bounded below by c * sd(lambda-bar^T F) / sqrt(G)-scaled quantity. Prop 3 (adjusted NPMLE): estimate F from the donor x gene residual matrix (PCA), deconvolve after removal, with an oracle inequality conditional on F. Prop 3 is the new-looking piece; Props 1-2 look like restatements of the Efron / Sun-Stephens pseudo-inflation phenomenon in different notation.
kept.data_test: Not run (per-donor gene-level skill estimates needed; local files hold only gene-level means: c0_gene_diagnostics.csv has r_within and R2c_mean averaged over donors). Plan on Longleaf outputs: per-donor, per-gene r_within for 50 (Visium) and 343 (Xenium) genes; bootstrap over donors (not genes) of the NPMLE fraction-above-c; compare spread with the gene-bootstrap spread to read off J_eff. Prediction: donor-bootstrap SD of the fraction of genes with r_within > 0.3 on LUNG_XENIUM is several times the gene-bootstrap SD. Local fact supporting dependence across genes: gene-wise r_within is rank-1 across encoders (PC1 share 0.93-0.98 over 6 tasks, checked from the CSV).

kept.title: What can be certified about a new group's risk without its labels? Identified versus hidden location/scale components under group shifts that are independent of X, with a finite-K certificate for the hidden part
kept.core_claim: For a frozen predictor f_hat, the risk on a new donor g splits into (i) a part determined by the donor's covariate law P_g(X) and the source residual structure, which labels are not needed to estimate, and (ii) a hidden block B_g = (a_g, s_g) of group-level location (the shared depth/detection offset) and noise-scale shifts that are statistically independent of X_g and therefore invisible to any label-free diagnostic, including embedding outlyingness. The claim is that (a) the label-free-identifiable functionals can be characterised exactly (offset-invariant, scale-invariant ones: centred risk up to scale, within-group rank metrics, group ranking of encoders if B_g is shared), (b) no label-free procedure can certify the rest, with a sharp lower bound, and (c) with K labelled donors the hidden block can be certified with an explicit K-dependent width, which exposes when the Jin-Egami-Rothenhausler rule 'covariate shift bounds conditional shift' fails (direction-specific technical offsets).
kept.formal_result_sketch: Model: Y_gi = f(X_gi) + a_g + s_g*eps_gi, (a_g, s_g) drawn across groups independently of the X-law P_g; covariate shift P_g arbitrary with overlap. Prop 1 (identification): the density-ratio / outcome-regression functional of squared source residuals identifies R_g^X = E_{P_g}[(f - f_hat)^2] and the centred risk of f_hat up to the unidentified scale; (a_g, s_g) are not identified: for any label-free procedure the minimax error over B-laws with the same P_g(X) is at least half the range of {a^2 + s^2 sigma^2}. Prop 2 (what is identified): invariance class = functionals of (Y_g - mean Y_g) / s_g, e.g. within-group correlation and encoder rank order when B_g is common to encoders. Thm (finite-K certificate): with LOGO estimates of (a_k^2, s_k^2) from K donors (each with n_k spots, noise inflated by spatial effective n), a deconvolved upper bound on the new donor's hidden term at level 1-alpha with width explicit in K, skewness, and n_eff; two versions: distribution-free order statistic (needs K >= 1/alpha - 1) and a studentised version with t_{K-1}-type reference for K=4-24. Cor: the standardized-measure rule of Jin et al. is valid iff the hidden block is direction-neutral; a rank-1 shared offset gives a counterexample with explicit violation ratio. Assumes exchangeability of groups, independence of B_g from P_g, bounded fourth moments. Not proved here; I only checked the algebra of the decomposition and ran a pilot (below). Caution: the order-statistic certificate is a conformal/tolerance-type statement across donors, so only the decomposition and the identified-set characterisation can carry novelty, not the certificate itself.
kept.data_test: HEST (needs Longleaf, not run by me): for the 6 tasks x 3 encoders with leave-donor-out predictions, compute per donor (i) a label-free estimate of the X-explained centred risk and within-donor correlation (importance-weighted source residuals), (ii) the realised centred risk, offset^2 and scale. kept.title: Label-free comparison of frozen encoders on a new donor: risk differences are identified when the invisible part of the outcome is common, levels are not; bias of triple collocation under shared-training-noise errors
kept.core_claim: Write p_k = a_k S + e_k for encoder k's prediction and Y = S + V + eps, where V is the part of expression no encoder sees. If the e_k are mutually uncorrelated and uncorrelated with V + eps, covariances among three encoders' predictions identify each encoder's error variance relative to the common signal, so the MSE differences R_k - R_j are label-free identified on a new donor while the levels (which contain Var(V + eps), including the depth/detection factor) are not. The encoders are trained by the same ridge head on the same labels and see the same image, so errors are positively correlated; the claim is a closed-form bias of the estimates under correlated errors and sign-definite bounds on the ranking.
kept.formal_result_sketch: Triple collocation estimate sigma_hat_1^2 = Var(p_1) - Cov(p_1,p_2) Cov(p_1,p_3) / Cov(p_2,p_3). With error covariances Delta_ij and c_ij = a_i a_j Var(S) + Delta_ij, the bias is [a_1^2 Var(S) Delta_23 - a_1 Var(S)(a_2 Delta_13 + a_3 Delta_12) - Delta_12 Delta_13] / c_23 (I checked this identity numerically on random draws, three of three agree to 1e-10). Aims: (i) conditions on the sign pattern of Delta under which the TC ranking of encoders is preserved (e.g. nearly equal pairwise Delta); (ii) a finite-K, group-level statement: with K donors the within-donor TC ranking is a K-sample comparison with t_{K-1} critical values; (iii) with ten encoders, the identification of Delta by an over-identified one-factor model plus a shared-noise factor and a test of its fit. The identity itself is routine algebra; whether (i)-(iii) are new is unclear.

I found nothing on the application side that supplies a formal added-information test for histology encoders (STpath, bioRxiv 2026.03.17.711896, only reports feature-importance complementarity; HEST-style benchmarks use paired Wilcoxon on few images).
sharpened_claim_if_any: Drop T3 as a headline (it is Ibragimov-Mueller / Canay et al. / universal inference applied to cross-fitted losses) and T2 as a separate result (Escanciano-Parra + Shah-Peters). Keep one theorem: for ridge probes with proportional p/n and within-group-correlated samples, the exact asymptotic null mean of the Clark-West statistic under leave-one-group-out fitting, in closed form through ridge degrees of freedom and the small model's shrinkage bias, and with it (a) the asymptotic size distortion of the uncorrected donor-level t-test, and (b) a corrected, group-cross-fitted statistic whose null centre is zero, with a finite-G t_{G-1}/sign-flip guarantee stated under an explicit exchangeability-of-donors condition. Position it against Escanciano-Parra (no handicap formula, time series, no groups), Gauran et al. (empirical, i.i.d.), and the correlated-sample ridge theory (arXiv:2408.04607), which is the technical prerequisite. A cleaner sharpening that is more clearly new: a negative result showing that no studentized leave-one-group-out test of the nested null is uniformly valid at G=15-25 when p>G unless the handicap is corrected, but this would still need a proof.
value_assessment: Without T1 the claim is an assembly of known pieces and would not meet the 'formal result of its own' bar at NeurIPS/ICML/AISTATS or a top statistics journal. T1, if it holds with within-group correlation, is a genuine but thin result: a one-theorem addition (centre of an OOS statistic via deterministic equivalents), of proposition-plus-simulation size, closest in spirit to Bellec-Zhang's DoF adjustment, and the whole paper then depends on how clean the correlated-sample extension is. It could carry a short methods/theory paper at AISTATS or an econometrics/forecasting venue (J. Econometrics, JBES) if the group-dependence and finite-G part is done properly; it is unlikely to be a top-journal lead on its own. Scoop risk is moderate: the machinery is current (2024 correlated-sample ridge theory) and Escanciano-Parra is adjacent. Not recommended as the lead of the paper; reasonable as the formal core of a methods section if the applied ST/ACS results are strong.

verdict_reason: No single paper does the claim, but three of its four propositions reduce to published machinery. (Prop 1) Over-selection by the nuisance rank is the rank-inflation of the best-linear-predictor coefficient when an omitted dense low-rank factor is correlated with X. Bing-Ning-Xu (AoS 2022) state this in a random-design hidden-variable model: the identifiable coefficient is F = Psi + A B, a sparse part plus a dense rank-K part. If p >= G-1 and the group-indicator columns lie in span(X), then Y = X(B + C lambda') + E exactly, and the Bunea-She-Wegkamp / Bing-Wegkamp consistency theorems applied to the enlarged coefficient of rank r+1 give over-selection as a corollary. (Prop 2) Within-group rank consistency is the same theorems applied after projecting out group indicators (Frisch-Waugh). Wu-Zhang-Li-Zheng (JMVA 2025) already analyse rank-constrained estimation with group-specific intercept vectors a_i and r* = rank(B), with an oracle inequality for known groups. AMMI/GGE practice in agronomy removes environment main effects before choosing the number of multiplicative axes by CV (Dias-Krzanowski 2003). (Prop 3) Group-level sign-flip tests with few clusters, with a 2^q sign-change group and a resolution floor, are Canay-Romano-Shaikh / Cai et al. machinery; Winkler et al. (2015, 2020) give block-level sign flips and permutation tests for the number of canonical correlations. The smallest p-value 2^-(G-1) is a counting fact. (Prop 4) A lower bound on the excess error of pooled leave-one-group-out CV rank selection, in terms of the between-group coefficient and the shift covariance, was NOT found in print. CV bias under clustering (Rabinowicz-Rosset 2022), leave-one-cluster-out size selection for scalar GLMs (NICc 2025), CV inconsistency for RRR in the iid case (She-Tran 2019) and LOEO CV in G x E models (Hrachov-Piepho 2026) are all adjacent but do not state it. This absence rests on search, not proof.

sharpened_claim_if_any: Drop 'over-selects by exactly the nuisance rank w.p. -> 1' as a headline; it is an almost-immediate corollary of BSW/BW applied to the enlarged coefficient. A defensible sharper claim is the two-estimand statement: for G groups, p >= G-1 and group-level nuisance rank k, (i) the pooled penalised rank rule recovers r + min(k, rank absorbed) with absorption governed by an explicit signal-to-penalty threshold; (ii) pooled LOGO-CV does NOT target r but the new-group-predictable rank r_LOGO(G, shift covariance), for which an exact characterisation (not only a lower bound) is given and shown to differ from r by an explicit amount; (iii) within-group demeaned rank is the only one of the three that targets r; (iv) a finite-G exact test of the between-group rank with proved validity and a power statement. Framing risk: LOGO-CV targets prediction on a new group, so 'under-selection' relative to the within-group rank is a statement about estimand mismatch, and a reviewer may say CV is doing what it was asked to do. Ask for r_LOGO as a separate estimand.
value_assessment: At most a proposition or appendix, not a methods paper by itself at NeurIPS/ICML/AISTATS. The over-selection and within-rank results (Props 1-2) will be read as corollaries of Bunea-She-Wegkamp / Bing-Wegkamp plus Bing-Ning-Xu's identifiability of F = Psi + A B, fixed-effects projection and AMMI practice. The sign-flip test (Prop 3) is an application of Canay-Romano-Shaikh and Winkler block sign-flips, and the 2^-(G-1) floor is a counting fact. The only item that could carry a formal contribution is the LOGO-CV rank-selection characterisation (Prop 4 / its sharpened form). Even that is thin: it sits close to Rabinowicz-Rosset (CV bias under clustering), NICc (leave-one-cluster-out size selection) and the Shao-type inconsistency literature. It could be a self-contained short note or a section of a larger paper on evaluating donor-robust prediction; a top statistics journal is unlikely unless Prop 4 grows into a full theory of group-CV rank selection with matching upper and lower bounds. Verdict reflects a search that cannot see inside paywalled full texts (Econometrica, JASA, Crop Science) and does not prove absence.

verdict_reason: Every ingredient is in print under other vocabularies; I found no paper that combines them for predictive skill. (a) Identifying noise variance and signal from several aggregation scales is the two-scale / multi-scale realized-variance programme (Zhang-Mykland-Ait-Sahalia 2005, Zhang 2006, Aït-Sahalia-Mykland-Zhang 2011). Its cross-moment form is two-scales realized covariance (Zhang 2011), which is the Cov(P,Y|m) analogue. The variance-ratio test (Lo-MacKinlay 1988), Allan variance in metrology, Krige's volume-variance relation and the geostatistical nugget use the same moment structure, Var(m-sum) = m*unit + m(m-1)*cross. (b) The ceiling R2_max(A)=S/(S+tau^2/A) is Spearman-Brown / ICC(k) reliability of an average. In neuroscience it is the noise ceiling CCmax and normalised correlation (Hsu et al. 2004, Schoppe et al. 2016, Pospisil & Bair 2021). In organisational psychometrics, Bliese 1998 shows group-level correlation depends on group size through ICC(2) and gives an attenuation correction. (c) Ranking of predictors being invariant to noise in the target is Patton 2011 / Hansen-Lunde 2006 and the Meddahi R2 result; the ratio of correlations being noise-invariant is the same idea as disattenuation. (d) Correlation changing with aggregation scale is the MAUP (Gehlke-Biehl 1934, Yule-Kendall 1950, Openshaw 1983). (e) Bounds on unit-level association from aggregates are ecological-inference bounds (Duncan-Davis 1953; Cho-Manski; Monotone EI 2026). LP-with-polyhedral-shape-restrictions bounds appear in Econometric Reviews / arXiv 2403.07236. (f) The smallest skilful scale is Roberts-Lean FSS 2008. (g) The power trade-off between block size and number of blocks is the cluster-randomised optimal-design / design-effect literature (Raudenbush 1997), and the noise-vs-sampling trade-off in RV (Hansen-Lunde 2006). Closest ML-adjacent hit: Arambepola et al. 2022 (arXiv 2005.03604) asks exactly 'does aggregate-level CV tell you fine-scale skill' for Poisson disaggregation regression, but only by simulation. No paper found that states point identification or sharp bounds of cell-level predictor skill c0 from multi-block-size count data.

what_remains_open: (i) Nothing found that states, for a PREDICTOR of a latent field, the joint identification of cell-level skill c0, the unit-level noise tau^2 and the ceiling from the Var/Cov moment system across block sizes, with count (Poisson / overdispersed) noise. (ii) Own algebra, not found in print and not verified beyond my reading: with Cov(P,Y|m)=m*c0+m(m-1)*c1 and no intercept, two distinct block sizes already give a 2x2 linear system for (c0,c1), so '>=3 sizes' only buys over-identification and a specification test. This makes result (1) a short ANOVA / variance-component-type identification, not a theorem-grade result. (iii) Result (2) is Cauchy-Schwarz on the between-unit cross-covariance (|c1| <= sqrt(kappa_p*kappa_lambda)); the 'monotone-in-distance LP tightening' has structural analogues in the ecological-inference literature (2403.07236, Monotone EI) but I found no application to covariance-type skill. (iv) Result (3), consistency and variance of a two-scale estimator under a spatially correlated latent field with count noise and block-size variation, is not found for this model; it is the part with the most real statistical content, though TSRV theory under dependent noise (Aït-Sahalia-Mykland-Zhang 2011) and Zhang 2011 are templates. (v) Donor-level exchangeable-group intervals for scale curves and encoder efficiency eta_k(A), and the exogenous-block-size designs (Xenium re-aggregation, Visium nuclei count as a support instrument), are project-specific and I found no prior ST or PUMS treatment, but they are mostly application plus known clustering inference. (vi) Result (5) is the classical cluster-size versus number-of-clusters power trade-off; only its instantiation to predictor comparison under a ceiling is not found. Limits of this check: Semantic Scholar was rate-limited (HTTP 429 on every call), so forward citations of the anchors were NOT checked. arXiv keyword queries were weak. I cannot rule out a paper in econometrics / survey sampling / neuroscience methods that handles the Cov(P,Y|m) system under other notation.
sharpened_claim_if_any: A claim most likely to survive: a theorem-level treatment of the two-block-size (or multi-size) moment system for CROSS-covariance between a predictor and a count outcome. That means (a) identification of cell-scale skill and the ceiling under Poisson / quasi-Poisson noise with unknown, block-size-varying mean intensity (the mean-weighting m*mu term makes Var depend on the mean field, which the TSRV literature does not treat), (b) a CLT and optimal block-size pair when the latent field is spatially correlated (kappa depends on m through a variogram), where Zhang-style bias-variance results are not available off the shelf, and (c) a specification test of exchangeability from over-identification across >=3 sizes, plus the formal link that the correlation ratio of two predictors equals the ratio of their cell-scale skills only when the exchangeable cross-covariance c1 is common (this identifiability caveat, if verified, is the real content of 'invariance'). Frame the paper as 'two-scale covariation estimator for noisy count fields' with the ST application, not as a new ceiling or a new aggregation effect.
value_assessment: As stated, the claim is mostly taken: the ceiling and normalisation are noise-ceiling / Spearman-Brown / ICC(2) results, scale-dependence is MAUP, the identified set is Cauchy-Schwarz plus ecological-inference bounds, the two-scale estimator is Zhang et al. 2005 / Zhang 2011, and the smallest skilful scale is FSS. Results (1), (2) and (5) are at most propositions or appendix material. The remainder that could carry a stats-journal methods paper is result (3), a consistent, asymptotically normal two-scale estimator of cell-scale predictive covariance with count noise and a spatially dependent latent field, together with the sharper identification caveat in the sharpened claim. For NeurIPS / ICML / AISTATS it would be a thin fit unless the empirical finding (how encoder rankings and ceilings change across scales on Xenium / Visium / PUMS) is strong. Partly-open grade is arguable only for the component (3) combination; this check cannot certify it because forward citations were not checked.

verdict_reason: Each ingredient is in print in some form. (1a) Label-free estimation of the covariate-explained risk by density-ratio / outcome-regression of source residuals is the standard transportability-of-model-performance literature (Steingrimsson et al. AJE 2023; Morrison et al. 2022 doubly robust; sensitivity analysis by exponential tilt, Steingrimsson-Robertson-Dahabreh, Biometrics 2024), plus the ML statement that target accuracy is identified iff the shift assumptions pin down p_t(y|x) (Garg et al. ICLR 2022, Prop. 1). (1b) The 'rest is not identified' lower bound is the generic same-P(X) two-point / identified-set-midpoint argument (minimax decision = midpoint of identified set, Giacomini-Kitagawa-Uhlig; same-P_T(X) hard pair in arXiv:2607.18088 for classification); invariance of rankings to a common additive noise in the target is classical forecast-evaluation theory (Patton 2011). (3) A K-source-group certificate for a new group's random hidden quantity is the random-effects prediction interval (Higgins-Thompson-Spiegelhalter 2009; applied to model performance by Debray/Snell-type IPD meta-analyses) and hierarchical conformal prediction for unseen groups; nonparametric deconvolution has logarithmic minimax rates, so only parametric/moment versions can have explicit polynomial-in-K width. Not found in print: the specific (a_g, s_g) location-scale block model with the catalogue of identified vs. non-identified functionals and the exact half-range minimax bound, and any stated condition (direction-neutrality) or counterexample (rank-one shared offset) for the Jin-Egami-Rothenhausler rule. The latter is the only component with no match, but Jin et al.'s own derivation is already conditional on a random, dense, independent-perturbation model, so a neutrality condition is a refinement of an assumption they state, and a shared offset with zero covariate shift is an elementary counterexample.

verdict_reason: Prop 2 and Thm 3 are essentially in print; Prop 1 is an elementary exact refinement of results that are approximately in print. (i) Thm 3: Patton (2011, J. Econometrics 160, Props 3-4) already gives the necessary-and-sufficient characterisation of robust AND homogeneous losses; its family member b=-1 is h - s2 + s2*log(s2/h), i.e. the Poisson/KL deviance (homogeneous of degree 1), while the degree-ZERO member (b=-2) is QLIKE/Itakura-Saito, not Poisson. So the conjectured 'degree-zero iff Poisson/KL' statement contradicts Patton's classification as written; Fissler-Ziegel (EJS 2019, Sec 4.2) and Fissler-Lorentzen-Mayer (arXiv 2202.12780) repeat the homogeneous-Bregman/Tweedie characterisation; Amari (2009) gives a KL uniqueness result for Bregman-intersect-f-divergence. (ii) Prop 2: rankings that change with the units/scale of the target under non-homogeneous robust losses is Patton Prop 3(ii); 'profile out a multiplicative nuisance = condition on the total = multinomial' is classical (Birch 1963 / Palmgren 1981 / Baker 1994 multinomial-Poisson transformation; Hausman-Hall-Griliches 1984 conditional Poisson FE; Taddy 2015; Townes et al. 2019 for scRNA-seq UMI counts). (iii) Prop 1: not found in print in exact form (E log1p Poisson elasticity e(m)=m*h'(m) via the Poisson derivative identity, strictly increasing 0 to 1, with variance-share/ceiling consequences), but the qualitative content is in print: Cohn-Liu-Wardlaw (JFE 2022) give the approximate log1plus loading E[y|x]/(1+E[y|x]) on a multiplicative effect; Lun (2018), Townes (2019), Hafemeister-Satija (2019), Ahlmann-Eltze-Huber (2023) show depth/size-factor effects on log-pseudocount counts depend on gene mean; Chen-Roth (QJE 2024) prove unit-dependence of log1p; the ceiling is a noise-ceiling/ICC variance decomposition (Nakagawa et al. 2017 delta-method machinery). I did NOT find any paper combining a shared multiplicative donor factor, log1p, a mean-count-predictable loading and a per-gene R2 ceiling for image predictors. This is provisional: Lun 2018 and Cohn et al. full texts and Thakral-To theory sections were not read, Google Scholar was not available, and arXiv/Semantic Scholar APIs were repeatedly rate-limited.

(c) Caution on the claim as stated: Patton's classification puts Poisson/KL at homogeneity degree 1 and QLIKE at degree 0, so 'degree-zero requirement iff Poisson/KL' is inconsistent. My own quick numerical check (not literature) shows the scale-profiled Poisson deviance of a donor grows roughly linearly in that donor's total count (profiled loss ~ T*KL(shares)), so pooled rankings are weighted by s_d unless the loss is normalised by the donor total (KL of shares); invariance to the law of s_d therefore needs the normalised/degree-0 version. A correct, sharper Thm 3 would be about profile-then-normalise Bregman losses on the simplex, where Amari-type uniqueness of KL is the likely nearest result.
sharpened_claim_if_any: If anything is to be kept: (1) state Prop 1 as an exact lemma for mixed Poisson with explicit remainder, and present it as the Poisson-exact version of Cohn-Liu-Wardlaw's E[y]/(1+E[y]) factor, citing Lun 2018 / Chen-Roth for the qualitative phenomenon; (2) replace Thm 3 by a characterisation within Patton's robust-and-homogeneous family: ranking by donor-pooled profiled loss is invariant to the law of the donor scale iff the profiled loss is homogeneous of degree 0 after profiling (equivalently the total-normalised multinomial KL, or QLIKE when y>0), and state explicitly how it differs from Patton Prop 3 (random persistent scale with forecasts blind to it vs deterministic rescaling); (3) keep the finance analogue only as a remark unless a result on persistent random multiplicative proxy bias with non-trivial new content is proved.
value_assessment: Not enough on its own for a NeurIPS/ICML/AISTATS methods paper or a top statistics journal: Thm 3 is a re-derivation inside Patton (2011), Prop 2's profiling step is classical, and Prop 1 is a short exact refinement of a known approximation. As a proposition/appendix (or a diagnostic section) in an application-oriented HEST-1k paper it is defensible and useful because it gives a closed-form, testable prediction (loading vs mean count; per-gene between-donor ceiling) that I did not find in the spatial-transcriptomics or scRNA-seq literature. Risk: a reviewer from econometrics will immediately cite Patton 2011 / Chen-Roth / Cohn et al.; a reviewer from single-cell will cite Lun 2018 and Townes 2019.

JASA 2025, which includes a changepoint application), conditional independence of thinned counts given a latent Cox-process intensity (Leininger-Gelfand p-thinning CV, restated in arXiv:2609.17908), the fact that train/test counts become correlated when the mean is random (Neufeld Prop. 2, NB/gamma case), the equal-means-between-estimated-clusters test (Gao-Bien-Witten, Chen-Witten, count-splitting App. C), a continuum rather than equal-means null for post-clustering inference (Hivert et al., arXiv:2210.13172, non-spatial), post-selection CIs for a selected spatial region (arXiv:2506.11564), and the generic eps selection-vs-inference tradeoff (Neufeld JMLR; Fithian-Sun-Taylor). RD/boundary-discontinuity machinery with robust bias correction exists only for a KNOWN boundary (Cattaneo-Titiunik-Yu) or an unknown cutoff estimated on the same data (Porter-Yu). I found NO paper that combines (thin -> estimate boundary on Y1 -> RD-type local-linear/RBC test on Y2) for a latent random field, none that derives size inflation of the form alpha + O(h*E|grad|/se) from selection on Y1, none with a bandwidth rule restoring size at an estimated boundary, and none with an optimal-eps result for boundary localisation vs RD power. Parts (2)-(4) are therefore not found in print, but they are a technical remainder on top of taken machinery, and the search was incomplete (see deviations).

what_remains_open: Not found in any retrieved source: (a) a formal statement that, for counts driven by a CONTINUOUS latent field, the between-domain difference-in-means test on held-out thinned counts rejects with probability -> 1 (so the estimand must be continuity of lambda at Gamma-hat) in the spatial setting [the mechanism is Neufeld Prop. 2 plus the continuum argument of Hivert et al., so this is a short corollary]; (b) a size-distortion expansion for a local-linear boundary-discontinuity statistic evaluated at a boundary selected on an independent thinned copy, with explicit dependence on field range, h, eps, n; (c) a bandwidth/RBC rule that restores size at a Y1-selected boundary; (d) an optimal-eps theorem balancing boundary-localisation error against RD power. Also not found: any direct application to Visium/Xenium domains, remote-sensing change detection, or finance order flow in this form. Caveats on the claim's own technical content: with Gamma-hat measurable in Y1 and Y2 conditionally independent of Y1 given lambda, the test is an ordinary RD test at a fixed curve conditional on lambda, so the distortion is the usual RD smoothing bias driven by the random field's local regularity; for local-LINEAR estimation that bias is O(h^2 x curvature), not O(h x gradient) (O(h x gradient) is the local-constant/difference-in-means case); and for a Matern field with smoothness <= 1 the gradient does not exist, so the rate would be h^nu-type. Marginally over lambda, Y1 and Y2 are dependent, so 'valid' must be defined conditional on lambda or the null is not the one the user wants. I did not verify any of these theoretical points; they are reading-based observations.
sharpened_claim_if_any: Model the field as lambda = smooth Matern/Gaussian component + optional jump across an unknown curve Gamma0. Define the null as no jump at the Y1-selected curve (continuity), and the estimand as the local-linear jump at bandwidth h conditional on lambda. Then state (i) the exact type-I error of the Y2-based local-linear/RBC test as a function of the field's smoothness nu, range, h, eps and the selection rule (selection on Y1 favours steep/high-curvature locations, so E[bias | Gamma-hat selected] exceeds the unconditional bias), (ii) a bandwidth rule h(eps, n, nu) giving asymptotic size alpha uniformly over Gamma-hat in a class, and (iii) a detection-boundary result (minimax or phase-transition in jump size vs eps, n, range) giving the optimal eps. The defensible new content is (i)-(iii) jointly for a RANDOM field with estimated boundary; the thinning step and the equal-means failure are not new.
value_assessment: As a NeurIPS/ICML/AISTATS methods paper the remainder is thin: the thinning/selection framework is Neufeld-Dharamshi-Gao-Witten, the continuity-vs-equal-means point is a corollary with a non-spatial precedent (Hivert et al.), and the RD/RBC machinery is Cattaneo-Titiunik-Yu. A paper stands only if (i)-(iii) are proved with nontrivial rates for random fields and estimated boundaries (a Biometrika/JRSSB/Annals-of-Applied-Statistics-style methods-theory note is more plausible than a main-track ML venue). As a stand-alone contribution inside the larger project it is a proposition/section plus simulation, not a headline result. The ST application is weakly motivated for HEST-1k because the project's labels are log1p counts with a donor depth factor, not raw counts, so the Poisson-thinning step does not apply to the main data without extra assumptions.

(i) Plug-in conditional/hybrid winner intervals: Andrews-Kitagawa-McCloskey (QJE 2023, known Sigma, uniform asymptotics with consistently estimated Sigma bounded away from singularity), McCloskey 2024, Zrnic-Fithian LSI (2212.09009) and zoom correction (2411.18569, arbitrary dependence, winner value AND index, top-k, near-winners), Petrou-Zeniou & Shaikh (2410.19212, set of ranked winners, degenerate Sigma allowed, studentised max), Bakshi-Gao-Gao-Panigrahi (2607.18545, Jul 2026, conditional winner CIs with a leaderboard application). (ii) Fixed-G validity of group-level resampling: Canay-Santos-Shaikh (wild bootstrap, fixed number of clusters, sign-change randomization), Cai-Canay-Kim-Shaikh, Ibragimov-Mueller, and sign-flip tests defined for d>n (Hemerik-Goeman-Finos); the zoom paper explicitly accepts ANY simultaneous region (exact error law or union bound), so a sign-flip/multiplier max-t region plugged into zoom/LSI is a direct corollary, not a new theorem. Multiplier-bootstrap max with p>>n is CCK 2013 (asymptotic in n). (iii) The M-free envelope when the covariance has rank <= G-1 is the classical Scheffe/Working-Hotelling/union-intersection geometry; rank <= n-1 with markers > samples and M_eff heuristics are discussed in genomics (arXiv:1612.04535). (iv) Efficiency of correlation versus union bound: Hsu MCB / Edwards-Hsu multivariate-t critical values, White RC/Hansen SPA/Romano-Wolf/MCS bootstraps, M_eff (Li-Ji, Nyholt), and very recently Yang & Chen (2609.28177, Sep 2026): equicorrelated Gaussian max with Slepian floor, k correlated tries ~ n_eff<k independent, and the observation that resampling subjects as blocks moves the relevant correlation from 0.46 to 0.92. Coverage is by abstract/snippet for most older econometrics papers and by keyword-targeted reading of the extracted text for 8 papers; I did NOT find a paper that studies finite-G coverage of plug-in conditional/hybrid winner intervals when the estimated covariance is rank-deficient (M>G), nor a minimax lower bound for that regime. The M-free envelope itself is classical; a sharp lower bound would be a corollary-level proposition. WARNING: when candidate directions are dense on the sphere the Scheffe envelope is not conservative, so (iii) as phrased ('conservativeness unavoidable when M>G') is false in that case and must be restated as a worst-case-over-structures statement. (c) The eigen-regularisation of a rank-deficient Sigma-hat inside a studentised max-t is not in the sources I read, but it is an implementation choice; a sign-flip or Hotelling-envelope region avoids covariance estimation altogether. (d) Application-level statistical content: a donor-level winner estimand for HEST-Bench-type metrics; no pathology/ST benchmark paper retrieved does winner inference (they use patient bootstraps and pairwise tests).

area: STSTAT: statistical methodology for spatial omics (excluding PPI and conformal)

problems.title: Post-selection tests for estimated spatial domain boundaries under a latent-field continuity null (count splitting + boundary-discontinuity statistic)
problems.source_and_stated_gap: ClusterDE (PMC10401959; Discussion): its synthetic null assumes a single homogeneous domain and the authors list gaining power while holding FDR as future work. Data fission/thinning limitations paper (arXiv:2405.13591, Discussion): thinning assumes a homogeneous distribution, i.e. no true clusters, so mixture structure is needed. MM-test (arXiv:2603.09061, Discussion): cluster-then-test gives invalid p-values (double dipping). Paraphrase of the shared gap: no valid p-value for 'is this estimated spatial domain boundary real' when spatial dependence is present and true domains exist.
problems.formulation: Y_i ~ Poisson(s_i * lambda(x_i)) with latent random field lambda (Matern, unknown range) and depth s_i. Thin Y into Y1=Bin(Y,eps), Y2=Y-Y1, independent given (lambda,s) even though lambda is spatially dependent. Estimate a boundary Gamma-hat from Y1 with any spatially smoothed clusterer. Test on Y2 the continuity null H0: lambda has no jump across Gamma-hat, using a local-linear boundary-discontinuity statistic with bandwidth h. The naive between-domain mean test is NOT valid even with perfectly independent folds, because under a continuous random field domains differ in mean; the null must be continuity, not equal means.
problems.formal_result_aim: (1) Proposition: the between-domain test rejects with probability -> 1 under a continuous Matern field; (2) Theorem: type-I error of the boundary-discontinuity test at a Y1-selected boundary is alpha + O(h*E|grad lambda(Gamma-hat)|/se), where selection on Y1 favours steep-gradient locations, giving explicit inflation in (range, h, eps, n); (3) a robust-bias-corrected version with a bandwidth rule restoring size; (4) optimal thinning fraction eps trading boundary-localisation error against test power (rate result).
problems.data_test: Visium CCRCC (24 donors) and INDIANA_KIDNEY (25 donors), raw counts and coordinates for the 50 genes. (a) Null calibration: fit Poisson-lognormal Matern fields per gene and slide, simulate continuous null fields at the real coordinates, compare naive, count-split-between-domain and boundary-discontinuity tests. (b) Real-data rejection rates versus eps, reported per donor. (c) Xenium lung (343 genes, near single-cell) for the fine-scale case, and re-aggregation to Visium-sized spots for a resolution check. Donor is the replicate; avoid donor-level few-cluster inference claims (excluded topic).
problems.scoop_check: Queries (arXiv, Crossref, web; see mine_STSTAT_queries.csv, 10 on this problem): count splitting spatial, data thinning random field, post-clustering inference spatial, RD with estimated cutoff, geographic RD unknown boundary, SI change point. Closest: Neufeld et al. count splitting (arXiv:2207.00554; NB version arXiv:2307.12985), Dharamshi et al. generalized thinning (arXiv:2303.12931), SI for clustering pipelines (arXiv:2603.18413), SI for change points (arXiv:1706.00514, 2104.12022, 2110.08989), Bayesian RD with unknown cutoff (10.1214/25-ba1575), rd2d and SpatialRDD (CRAN), spatial RDD under spillovers (10.2139/ssrn.7266687), wombling, ClusterDE. I found no paper that combines thinning of a latent-field count process with boundary-discontinuity inference at a data-selected spatial boundary. Caveats: arXiv phrase search is weak for this topic, Semantic Scholar was rate-limited so not used, and a SpatialLens query on count splitting for spatial DE in the digest (section C) returned nothing but was ungraded. Each component is published; only the combination and the gradient-selection inflation result are unseen.
problems.finance_transfer: Regime/structural-break detection followed by inference on a held-out thinned fold (Poisson order-flow or trade counts); regression-discontinuity with an estimated cutoff; geographic RD in econometrics; change detection in remote sensing.

problems.title: Identification and valid tests of neighbour (context) effects under transcript spillover, calibrated with negative-control genes
problems.source_and_stated_gap: Nature Genetics segmentation-error paper (10.1038/s41588-025-02497-4; Discussion): residual admixture remains after correction, and a sufficiently powered downstream test will rediscover it, so downstream methods should explicitly control for segmentation errors. smiDE (10.1186/s13059-025-03867-1; Discussion): heuristic covariate adjustment/gene filtering for misassignment, spatial confounding unresolved. MisTIC (PMC12724677; Discussion): effectiveness depends on initial boundary quality and gives no per-cell confidence. Spacelink (bioRxiv 10.1101/2025.09.24.678397; Limitations 7): single-cell platform results depend on segmentation quality.
problems.formulation: Observed y_i^g = (1-a_i) x_i^g + a_i * sum_j w(d_ij) x_j^g + noise, x = true own-cell expression, w a distance-decay spillover kernel. Estimand: theta_g = effect of neighbour cell-type composition on the focal cell's own expression of gene g. Naive regression targets theta_g + a * (cross-type expression contrast), a bias that does not vanish with n. Negative-control genes (zero true expression in the focal type, e.g. mutually exclusive markers) identify a(d). Questions: sharp partial-identification set for theta_g without controls, point identification and asymptotic normality with controls and estimated a(d), and false-positive rate of the naive test as a function of leakage fraction.
problems.formal_result_aim: Identification theorem (negative-control gene set of size >= 1 per focal type suffices under a monotone-kernel assumption), bias formula and false-positive-rate bound for the naive test, sandwich variance accounting for estimated a(d), and a lower bound on the control-gene count needed for size control.
problems.data_test: Xenium lung (15 donors, 343 genes, near single-cell): (i) semi-synthetic injection of known spillover with a chosen kernel at cell level (ground truth known) to check bias formula and coverage; (ii) real data: estimate leakage decay of focal-type marker genes into neighbours using centroids and nuclear morphology as a cell-size proxy; (iii) compare naive and corrected neighbour-effect tests with donors as replicates (descriptive only).
problems.scoop_check: Queries (12 logged): transcript misassignment/negative control/spillover in ST (web, arXiv, Crossref), ambient RNA decontamination, spatial moving-average outcome error, peer-effects measurement error. ST side found only correction methods: Mitchel et al. NMF+CRF, Ergen & Yosef probabilistic diffusion, Wu/Beechem/Danaher CosMx reassignment (all as described in the Nat Methods Xenium paper 10.1038/s41592-026-03089-8, excerpts only), MisTIC, smiDE; also ambient-RNA decontamination benchmark 10.64898/2026.01.13.699237 (title only). Econometrics side: measurement error and peer effects in networks (arXiv:2608.00336; noisy proxies can inflate peer effects, identification via network structure), SAR with covariate measurement error (arXiv:2402.04593), spatially correlated measurement error (10.21203/rs.3.rs-9706755/v1; abstract not read). Those treat covariate error, not outcome contamination by neighbours' latent outcomes with exclusion genes. Risk: a referee may see this as proximal/negative-control reasoning applied to a spatial moving-average outcome, so the theory contribution could be judged incremental.
problems.finance_transfer: Non-synchronous trading and stale-price mixing of returns across neighbouring assets, spillover/contagion estimates with contaminated outcomes, negative-control assets (placebo portfolios) for calibration.

problems.title: Valid cell-type-specific spatial tests when composition is a deconvolution estimate: generated simplex regressors with spatially correlated error
problems.source_and_stated_gap: Celina (Nat Commun 10.1038/s41467-025-56280-4; Discussion, limitation 1): accuracy depends on deconvolution accuracy, power ordering true > CARD > RCTD; also reports CSIDE p-values inflated (genomic inflation 1.23-4.12). Spacelink (limitation 5): cell-type version relies on spot-level proportions, errors from poorly matched references propagate into inference. FlashDeconv (PMC12776147; Limitations): reference incompleteness biases estimates.
problems.formulation: y_s ~ NB(mu_s), log mu_s = sum_k pi_sk beta_gk + f_g(x_s), but only pi-hat_s = pi_s + e_s is available, e_s on the simplex, spatially smooth, covariance depending on pi_s and reference mismatch. Test beta_gk = c or a cell-type-specific spatial variance component. Question: size distortion of Wald/score tests that plug in pi-hat, in particular spurious spatial variance attributed to type k because e_s is itself spatially structured.
problems.formal_result_aim: Murphy-Topel-type correction of the covariance for a spatial GLMM with generated simplex regressors; size-distortion bound in terms of error covariance and its spatial spectrum; a calibrated test valid under a bounded-error-covariance class; identification bound on beta when only ||e|| is bounded.
problems.data_test: Xenium lung: define cell types from marker genes, aggregate cells to Visium-sized pseudo-spots to obtain ground-truth pi_s, run a reference-based deconvolution (reference from other donors) for pi-hat_s, then compare type-I error and power of cell-type-specific tests using true versus estimated pi under a permuted-effect null. 15 donors serve as replicate experiments.
problems.scoop_check: Queries (9 logged): generated regressors/cell-type proportions (arXiv), errors-in-variables deconvolution, estimated proportions downstream tests, Murphy-Topel two-step, ct-SVG error propagation, compositional covariates with measurement error. Closest: generated-regressor inference in econometrics (10.2139/ssrn.7493339; 10.2139/ssrn.7153809), inference on proportions estimated from bulk data (JASA 10.1080/01621459.2024.2382435, no abstract retrieved), a bulk measurement-error-adjusted deconvolution framework seen only as a ResearchGate snippet, ctSVG (10.21203/rs.3.rs-5655066/v1) and STANCE (10.1101/2024.09.22.614385), both of which plug in estimated composition. I found no treatment of spatially structured simplex error for ST tests. Risk: the non-spatial core is classical generated-regressor theory, so novelty rests on the spatial error structure and the simplex constraint.
problems.finance_transfer: Two-step Fama-MacBeth and generated regressors in asset pricing; estimated portfolio or style weights (simplex) used as regressors; factor-exposure error propagation.

problems.title: Spatially variable gene tests with a spatially structured, partially observed depth/composition nuisance: estimand, null and robust calibration
problems.source_and_stated_gap: SVG benchmark (Genome Biol 10.1186/s13059-025-03731-2; Discussion): most methods give poorly calibrated p-values; authors advise rank thresholds instead of significance. Multi-scale testing (PMC13015534; limitations): moment matching cannot capture tail behaviour of zero-inflated quadratic forms, saddlepoint approximation could tighten calibration. Spacelink (limitation 2): residual capture-efficiency differences across platforms. smiDE: spatial confounding with structured covariates.
problems.formulation: Y_ig ~ Poisson(s(x_i) * lambda_g(x_i)), depth field s latent and smooth, proxied by library size L_i = sum_g Y_ig, which contains signal. H0_g: lambda_g constant. Normalising by L_i can induce spatial structure in null genes when many programmes vary spatially (compositional effect). Estimate s from negative-control genes; study tests conditional on s-hat. Target: size distortion as a function of the spatial-frequency error of s-hat, and a Monte Carlo (field-fitted) null that is robust to it.
problems.formal_result_aim: Non-identification statement (when s and lambda_g share spatial frequencies only a ratio is identified), bound on size distortion of quadratic-form SVG statistics in terms of ||s-hat - s|| in a spectral norm, and a robust Monte Carlo calibration with finite-sample validity under a TV-distance misspecification budget.
problems.data_test: Visium 50-gene tasks (raw counts, coordinates): the project already finds a shared donor-level depth factor holding 0.650 of between-donor variance on CCRCC; here study the within-slide depth field. Compare calibration on cyclic-shift/permutation nulls for normalised versus conditional tests. Xenium lung: cell-level versus aggregated counts to isolate the composition effect.
problems.scoop_check: Queries (7 logged, Crossref/arXiv, mostly weak): CRT/permutation under spatial confounding, library size as confounder in SVG, restricted randomisation for autocorrelated fields, robust CRT under misspecification. Closest: SVG benchmark, SOAAR (10.64898/2026.07.06.736800, abstract only: autocorrelation-preserving resampling for gene-gene correlation tests), a title raising the library-size question empirically (10.1101/2025.09.15.676443, 'Library Size in Spatial ATAC-seq: Technical Confounder or Biology?', abstract not read), multi-scale test. The topic is poorly covered by arXiv/Crossref, so a missed prior is plausible, especially in the geostatistics literature on testing correlation between autocorrelated fields and in the spoon-type SVG normalisation papers (not retrieved).
problems.finance_transfer: Testing cross-sectional structure after removing a latent market/liquidity factor observed through a proxy that contains signal; conditional independence tests with an estimated confounder.

problems.title: Scale decomposition identity for image-predicted expression: what Moran's I and per-gene PCC of predictions can certify
problems.source_and_stated_gap: Histology-prediction benchmark (PMC13445978; Methods/Discussion): introduces a Moran-inspired spatial metric, reports PCC only 0.1-0.3. Active-spot benchmark (arXiv:2609.27208; Discussion and Future Work): PCC/ARI reversal not reproduced on a second cohort, comparisons descriptive, pointwise and spatial measures should be reported separately. A published prediction paper reports Moran's I of its predictions as evidence of validity (FOCST, PLOS Comput Biol 10.1371/journal.pcbi.1014762, search excerpt).
problems.formulation: For a predictor yhat = f(image features) on a spatial graph, decompose PCC and Moran's I over graph-Fourier scales; relate I(yhat) to I(y) and to residual spatial autocorrelation; give conditions under which I(yhat) exceeds I(y) (smoother predictor) and when scale-resolved correlation is identified from within-donor data.
problems.formal_result_aim: An exact scale-decomposition of PCC, bounds on I(yhat) versus I(y), and a donor-level bootstrap or sign-flip interval for scale-resolved skill.
problems.data_test: Per-spot leave-donor-out ridge predictions with labels for 6 tasks x 3 encoders, with coordinates: compute scale-resolved correlation and Moran's I of predictions versus labels; Xenium lung (within-donor correlation 0.52-0.63) as a high-skill contrast.
problems.scoop_check: Queries (5 logged). Closest and decisive: Octave (10.64898/2026.09.25.754484, Oct 2026, abstract only) states PCC does not distinguish spatial scales and builds a domain oracle and scale-resolved evaluation; kriging smoothing-effect literature is classical (queries did not retrieve it, so I cite none). The digest also lists related excluded ideas (SCALE, signature plot, gene-gene correlation inflation in predictions). Remainder is theory for Moran's I of predictions and donor-level intervals, which looks thin.
problems.finance_transfer: Frequency-resolved forecast evaluation (skill by horizon/scale), smoothness bias of forecasts versus realised variation.

problems.title: Spatial confounding in cell-type or domain differential expression when the covariate is a spatially structured label
problems.source_and_stated_gap: smiDE (10.1186/s13059-025-03867-1; Discussion): spatial confounding when the covariate has strong spatial structure (niches, regions) is a key limitation; joint multi-sample spatial modelling is the next step.
problems.formulation: y_s = x_s' beta + w(s) + e with x_s a label (cell type or domain) correlated with the Gaussian random field w; question: what GLS/restricted-spatial-regression estimators target when the label was itself derived from expression, and the identifiable beta under smoothness mismatch.
problems.formal_result_aim: Characterisation of the bias of beta under label-derived covariates; probably only an adaptation of existing spatial-confounding results.
problems.data_test: Visium tasks: domain labels from image-only clustering versus expression-derived clustering, compare beta estimates and calibration; Xenium lung cell-type labels.
problems.scoop_check: Queries (2 logged). Closest: Spatial self-confounding (Biometrika 10.1093/biomet/asaf076; abstract only), Demystifying Spatial Confounding (arXiv:2309.16861; Environmetrics 10.1002/env.70128), Spatial+ (10.1007/s13253-023-00586-7), TESSERA for multi-sample (10.64898/2026.04.27.720955). Fully occupied by statistics literature; only an ST application remains.
problems.finance_transfer: Omitted-factor bias with smooth latent confounders in cross-sectional return regressions.

problems.title: CKA-DONOR: donor-aware, bias-corrected and exactly calibrated representation similarity (CKA) between frozen encoders when spots are nested in few donors
problems.source_and_stated_gap: Groger, Wen, Brbic (arXiv:2602.14486), "Limitations and outlook": the calibrated/debiased similarity guarantees assume exchangeability, so grouped or clustered samples require restricted permutations that preserve the dependence structure (stated, not done). Corroboration: PathoROB (arXiv:2507.17845) finds centre information pervasive in 20 pathology-FM embeddings; CRoMa (arXiv:2607.25497) lists needing known confounder labels as a limitation.
problems.formulation: Spots i nested in donors g(i), G=5-25 donors; encoder features X_i, Y_i. Target = donor-population similarity, not spot-population. Centred cross-covariance splits exactly as C = C_B + C_W (between-donor means, within-donor deviations; X_B^T Y_W = 0), so linear HSIC = ||C_B||^2 + ||C_W||^2 + 2<C_B,C_W> (identity checked numerically on random data: between share 0.80, within 0.13, cross 0.07). Estimands: pooled CKA, within-donor CKA, between-donor CKA, and their ratio form; null = no alignment beyond donor structure.
problems.formal_result_aim: (i) Exact expectation of the standard unbiased-HSIC CKA under a donor random-effects model (bias as an explicit function of ICC and n_g, not zero); (ii) a cross-donor-pair U-statistic estimator unbiased for the donor-population HSIC with sqrt(G) CLT and delta-method/studentised CKA ratio; (iii) a donor-block permutation (or sign-flip) test with exact finite-sample level for exchangeable donors, valid for G as small as 1/alpha-quantile allows, plus power as a function of (G, n_g); (iv) impossibility/conservativeness statement for unequal n_g.
problems.data_test: 10 encoders x 10 HEST tasks (3-25 donors), 45 encoder pairs: compare pooled vs within-donor CKA and test with donor-block permutations; prediction to test: pooled CKA is inflated by donor/site fingerprint while within-donor CKA is much lower, and the rank-one gene skill structure (PC1 share 0.93-0.98) is a within-donor phenomenon. Toy check done here (provisional, G=10, n=50 per donor, d=20, independent donor offsets, 60 reps x 99 permutations): global-permutation CKA test rejected 100% at nominal 5% (tau=0.5 and 1.0) while donor-block permutation rejected 3-5%; both 5% with no donor effect.
problems.scoop_check: Independence-test half is TAKEN: Liu et al. NeurIPS 2021 and the Sci Rep 2022 fast version give HSIC tests for cluster-correlated data (asymptotic null, large-cluster regime). Also: Schutt et al. eLife 2023 (2-factor bootstrap for RSA with subjects and stimuli random effects), Chwialkowski et al. arXiv:1408.5404 (wild bootstrap for dependent data), Murphy 2405.01012 and Chun 2502.15104 (debiased CKA for i.i.d. samples), Groger 2602.14486 itself. Not found: CKA (ratio) estimand under donor nesting with between/within split, few-donor exact calibration, or any histology-encoder application. The algebraic decomposition is trivial; novelty would rest on (ii)-(iii). 10 web + 5 arXiv/other queries.
