problems.title: WINNER-FEW: inference on the winning encoder/configuration when candidate losses are near rank-one dependent and the covariance is estimated from G donors
problems.source_and_stated_gap: Zrnic & Fithian (arXiv:2411.18569), Discussion: the hybrid method is the most powerful when a normal approximation with known covariance is available, struggles with many clearly suboptimal candidates, and the zoom correction reverts to a union bound under unknown dependence. Bakshi et al. (arXiv:2607.18545) list power gains without extra conditioning and follow-up questions as future directions; Xu et al. (arXiv:2605.05973) leave open-ended adaptive search to future work; Andrews-Kitagawa-McCloskey and the multiple-winners paper (arXiv:2410.19212) treat the covariance as known.
problems.formulation: Candidates m=1..M (10 encoders, optionally x PCA dimension x ridge penalty); donors d=1..G are i.i.d. units with per-donor skill vector s_d in R^M; theta_m = E s_{d,m}; winner m_hat = argmax of the donor-mean. Targets: theta_{m_hat}, the identity set of population winners, and the gap to the runner-up. Sigma_hat has rank <= G-1 and entries near 1 (rank-one skill).
problems.formal_result_aim: (i) Finite-G coverage error of plug-in hybrid/conditional winner intervals as a function of M/G and the correlation spectrum; (ii) a studentised max-t with donor-level multiplier calibration and eigen-regularisation that is provably valid for fixed G and M>G; (iii) a lower bound showing conservativeness is unavoidable when M exceeds G unless correlation is exploited; (iv) the efficiency gain from near rank-one dependence (width shrinks relative to union bound).
problems.data_test: Per task, select the best of the 10 encoders on a random half of donors and evaluate on the other half to measure the realised winner curse; compare naive, union-bound, zoom, hybrid and the new interval on the 10 HEST tasks (3-25 donors) and the 6 tasks x 3 encoders prediction files; coverage checked by donor-split resampling (necessarily at reduced G).
problems.scoop_check: Occupied at generic level: Andrews et al. (conditional/hybrid), Zrnic-Fithian, Bakshi et al., SIREN (adaptive benchmarking), Wei et al. arXiv:2206.11868 (estimated covariance, growing dimension). Classical multiple-comparison-with-the-best procedures (reality-check, superior-predictive-ability, model-confidence-set families) are known to me but were NOT retrieved in this session and must be verified. No cluster-level treatment with G<M or rank-one dependence found in 2 targeted web queries. Adjacent to excluded BENCH: it differs because the target is selected-winner inference (selection bias), not the pairwise encoder difference.
problems.finance_transfer: Strong: backtest overfitting, best strategy among many with few independent time blocks (blocks play the role of donors), estimated covariance among strategies; deflated-Sharpe-type problems.

problems.title: SPECSHARE: debiased inference on the rank and rank-one share of a model x gene/task skill matrix whose noise comes from shared test donors
problems.source_and_stated_gap: Low-rank evaluation papers fix rank heuristically or assume it and treat noise as i.i.d.: Maimon et al. (arXiv:2507.20208) pick the number of factors by the Kaiser rule and an 85 percent cumulative-variance threshold; Li, Simchi-Levi, Sun (arXiv:2605.29395, arXiv:2604.05460) assume a known rank with i.i.d. BTL comparisons and I found no explicit limitations passage; Hardy et al. (arXiv:2605.25272, search excerpt only) say benchmark noise sources and magnitudes remain unquantified. The gap is therefore my paraphrase of an omission, not an authors quoted limitation.
problems.formulation: S in R^{genes x encoders}: donor-population per-gene skill (e.g. within-donor correlation). Observed S_hat = mean over G donors of s_d, with noise E = S_hat - S dependent across genes and encoders through the shared donors. Estimands: rank r(S), top share rho_1 = sigma_1^2/||S||_F^2 (project data: PC1 share 0.93-0.98 across 3 encoders x 6 tasks), with and without removal of a donor-level nuisance factor.
problems.formal_result_aim: (i) Upward bias expansion of the naive rho_1 (order tr(Sigma_E)/(G ||S||_F^2)); (ii) split-donor cross-fitted estimator with CLT and cluster-multiplier-bootstrap CI valid for G->inf, fixed M, many genes; (iii) rank test (singular-value null rank r) with uniform validity; (iv) finite-G correction and a statement of when rank-one is identifiable from noise that is itself rank-one correlated.
problems.data_test: Gene x encoder matrices of within-donor correlation for 10 encoders on 10 tasks (50-gene Visium, 343-gene Xenium): naive vs debiased share, bootstrap CIs, split-donor replication; contrast with donor-mean R2 skill, where cross-gene agreement is much lower (Spearman 0.20-0.86), to see whether rank-one is a within-donor property.
problems.scoop_check: Generic problem occupied: factor-number selection under strongly correlated errors (Bai-Ng 2002, Ahn-Horenstein 2013, Onatski, Lam-Yao, Lin-Michailidis arXiv:1912.04123), bootstrap PCA eigenvalue CIs (Fisher et al. arXiv:1405.0922), Horn parallel analysis (used in arXiv:2602.15532), rank tests under noise (arXiv:2601.08353). Not found: resampling unit = test donor shared by all models/items, debiased spectral share in an evaluation matrix. Likely reduces to a corollary of cluster bootstrap plus a delta-method unless a sharp finite-G or identifiability result emerges. 3 web + 4 arXiv queries.
problems.finance_transfer: Strong: number of factors and first-factor share of a strategy x asset (or signal x period) performance matrix with block-dependent noise; Bai-Ng literature gives direct comparison.

problems.title: TWOLEVEL: two-level (donors x spots per donor) learning curves for frozen-encoder probes, with extrapolation intervals and an interchangeability boundary
problems.source_and_stated_gap: Nezhurina et al. (arXiv:2506.04598), Discussion: accurate scaling laws need dense small-scale measurements and fitting routines that extrapolate accurately (future work); Kricheli et al. (arXiv:2605.08541), Limitations: their theorem gives an ordering not a magnitude and the corollary assumes i.i.d. Gaussian residuals. Ooi et al. (Nature 2025, excerpts only) derive a sample-size versus scan-time model for connectome prediction; I did not read their limitations.
problems.formulation: Risk R(G,m) of a ridge probe trained on G donors with m spots each, tested on a new donor. Working model R = R_inf + a G^-alpha + b (G m)^-beta + donor-level term; targets alpha, the boundary m*(G) beyond which more spots per donor stop substituting for donors, the cost-optimal allocation, and the extrapolated risk at G* > G_obs. Learning-curve points use nested subsets of the same donors, hence are dependent.
problems.formal_result_aim: (i) Closed-form two-level learning curve for ridge on frozen features with donor random coefficients (deterministic-equivalent route); (ii) donor-level jackknife/bootstrap interval for extrapolated risk with coverage guarantee under the power-law model and nested-subset dependence; (iii) bias of leave-one-donor-out curves (training size G-1) and its correction; (iv) allocation rule.
problems.data_test: CCRCC (24 donors), INDIANA_KIDNEY (25), Xenium lung (15 donors, 343 genes, re-aggregable): vary G in 5..G-1 and m in 10..all; per-gene exponents, test whether exponents share a rank-one structure across the 10 encoders.

Formal novelty is thin; risk of being a mixed-model design-effect corollary. 3 web + 4 arXiv queries.

problems.title: EMBED-DML: transferability test and cluster-level cross-fitting for frozen-embedding controls when embeddings encode donor identity
problems.source_and_stated_gap: Shimizu (arXiv:2607.17378): uniform convergence rate over the estimated set of embedding functions, relaxing the strong density-ratio condition, and rates for regularised neural-network target estimators are left to future research; the multiplier-bootstrap transferability test is proven for a single nuisance-training block (the cross-fitted version needs a separate argument); the theory assumes an i.i.d. target sample, with requester clustering used only in the application.
problems.formulation: Partially linear model Y_i = theta X_i + g(E(W_i)) + U_i with E a frozen encoder (10 choices), observations nested in G donors; embeddings predict donor identity (PathoROB), so cross-fitted g can use donor fingerprints; theta = within-donor effect of a spot-level covariate (nuclear morphology) on expression.
problems.formal_result_aim: Neyman-orthogonal score with donor-level cross-fitting and donor demeaning; rate conditions split into between and within components; CLT with cluster-robust variance as G->inf, finite-G correction; a transferability/identification test across encoders under cluster dependence with cross-fitting.
problems.data_test: theta-hat across the 10 encoders for nuclear-morphology to expression on HEST tasks and Xenium lung (re-aggregated); the proposed test asks whether estimates differ across encoders beyond sampling error.
problems.scoop_check: Largely taken: multiway-cluster DML (Chiang et al. arXiv:1909.03489), panel DML with fixed effects (Clarke-Polselli arXiv:2312.08174; Fuhr-Papies arXiv:2409.01266), interactive-fixed-effects DML with N=20 units and cluster-robust variance (arXiv:2608.01137), subject-level block cross-fitting in software (arXiv:2512.15965 excerpt). problems.title: Limits-to-Learning lower bound on population R2 when noise has a shared unit-level (donor/period) component, validated on ground truth
problems.source_and_stated_gap: Chen, Kelly, Malamud, 'Limits To (Machine) Learning' (arXiv:2512.12735, Dec 2025). Assumption 1 (Sec 3) takes the noise eps_t iid and independent of signals and predictable component; the LLG lower bound R2* >= (R2_OOS + L)/(1+L) and its CLT (Thm 3) are derived under it. Stated gap (App. F, leave-for-future-research): the best feasible MSE needs estimation of Sigma_beta (the coefficient covariance), described as highly complex. The cluster-noise limitation is my reading of Assumption 1, not an author statement.
problems.formulation: y_dj = f(x_dj) + eta_d + e_dj, donors d=1..G, spots j=1..n_d, eta_d a donor-level shift (depth/detection factor) invisible to x, e_dj iid. Predictor = ridge or kernel ridge fitted leave-donor-out. Target: a data-driven lower confidence bound for the population R2 of f (within-donor part) and a separate bound for the between-donor part, as a function of leave-donor-out R2 and a computable gap L_c that uses G (not n) where eta enters.
problems.formal_result_aim: (i) Show the iid-noise LLG bound is invalid (over-claims) when var(eta)>0 and the fitted model is not demeaned by donor, with an explicit violation term; (ii) derive the cluster LLG L_c and prove a sqrt(G)-rate CLT for the corrected bound with n_d->infinity or n_d~p; (iii) a sharpness/impossibility statement when eta is correlated with x. All three are aims, none proved.
problems.data_test: Xenium lung (15 donors, 343 genes, 3 encoders): compute leave-donor-out R2 and iid vs cluster LLG per gene; ground-truth ceiling proxied by (a) re-aggregating cells to reduce Poisson noise and (b) donor learning curves; check empirical coverage of the lower bound across 343 genes. Visium CCRCC (24 donors, 50 genes), where the user reports the shared depth factor carries 0.650 of between-donor variance: the iid bound should fail at donor level and the cluster bound should hold. Finance cannot do this check because the population R2 is never observed. No data were touched in this mining run.
problems.scoop_check: 6 queries (web_search x2, arXiv API x3, Crossref x1; Semantic Scholar failed with 429). The only LLG paper found is the original (iid noise). Variance-component / SNR inference under p>n exists (EigenPrism arXiv:1505.02097; HEDE arXiv:2406.11184; multivariate SNR inference arXiv:2506.10370; misspecified mixed-model analysis, Jiang et al. AoS 2016) and the digest already holds a two-level EigenPrism idea (Repr B) and an embedding-heritability idea (Repr F). Difference from those: the object is a bound computed from out-of-sample R2 with a tuned ridge, not a variance-component estimate. Residual risk: a mixed-model argument may already give the cluster version in a line; I could not confirm that nothing exists, search quality of the APIs was poor.
problems.finance_transfer: Panel returns with a common period shock (market-wide) violate iid noise; same bound for factor-timing and cross-sectional R2 in Gu-Kelly-Xiu-type panels; supplies a finance-testable corrected LLG.

problems.title: Dense (non-sparse) reduced-rank ridge with many proxies: limiting factor-space recovery and prediction risk at p ~ n and p > n
problems.source_and_stated_gap: Wan, Li, Lu, Song, 'Mining the Factor Zoo: Estimation of Latent Factor Models with Sufficient Proxies' (arXiv:2212.12845; J. Econometrics 2024), Discussion, fourth point: the penalised reduced-rank regression avoids a sparsity assumption because lasso behaves poorly with correlated proxies, but without sparsity the theory at p ~ T is stated to be generally challenging and left as an extension.
problems.formulation: Y (n x q genes) = X B + E, rank(B)=r small, X (n x p embeddings) with general covariance, p/n -> gamma in (0,inf), q/n finite, ridge-regularised reduced-rank estimator B_hat(lambda, r). Quantities: limiting out-of-sample risk, alignment of the estimated r-dimensional response subspace with the true one, and optimal singular-value shrinkage.
problems.formal_result_aim: Deterministic-equivalent / free-probability limit of risk and subspace alignment of reduced-rank ridge with rotationally invariant or general-covariance X; an exact threshold in (gamma, signal spikes) below which proxy-based factor recovery beats PCA on Y alone; consistent data-driven choice of (lambda, r).
problems.data_test: Xenium lung: within-donor spots n_d in the thousands, p = embedding dimension of each of 10 encoders, q = 343 genes, so p/n is genuinely proportional; ground truth = held-out donor R2 per rank and per encoder, with nuclear morphology as a low-dimensional baseline. Also the digest fact that gene-wise skill is nearly rank-one across encoders gives a falsifiable prediction (r=1 should dominate).
problems.scoop_check: 3 queries (web_search x3). Closest: Dobriban-Wager arXiv:1507.03003 (single response ridge, proportional regime); Kargin arXiv:1409.6779 (reduced-rank regression with p, q, N proportional but N>=p and unpenalised; singular-value laws and rank selection); Bing-Wegkamp arXiv:1704.02381 and Bunea-She-Wegkamp (rank selection); Mukherjee-Zhu 2011 reduced-rank ridge (method, no limit theory found). The digest PRANK verdict (mostly_taken) concerns rank selection under a donor nuisance factor and leave-group-out CV; this problem differs in that it targets the ridge p>n limit of factor-space recovery with proxies, not selection. Not found does not mean absent: ML-theory papers on multi-output or deep linear ridge may contain it.
problems.finance_transfer: Factor-zoo proxy regression (p ~ T) and IPCA-style estimation of latent factors from many characteristics; gives risk limits that finance papers currently only simulate.

problems.title: Joint forecast-calibration (Mincer-Zarnowitz) test across N targets with small T and a strong common factor in the forecast errors
problems.source_and_stated_gap: Zhao, Ma, Feng, 'High dimensional alpha test ... Lq-norm' (arXiv:2603.29764, Sec 5): tests assume temporally independent observations, extension to dependent or conditional models left for future research; Chernov, Kelly, Malamud, Schwab (NBER w33565) extend GRS to N>T with ridge-regularised covariance (regressors common to all assets). In forecasting, Qu-Timmermann-Zhu panel/cross-sectional EPA tests handle small T but compare accuracy, not calibration. Stated gap about MZ with N>T is my synthesis, not a statement by those authors.
problems.formulation: For targets g=1..N and periods d=1..T (T < N, e.g. T=15-25, N=50-343): y_gd = a_g + b_g yhat_gd + u_gd, with equation-specific regressors yhat_gd and u_gd = lambda_g F_d + v_gd. Test H0: a_g=0, b_g=1 for all g, and the sparse alternative (few miscalibrated g).
problems.formal_result_aim: Null distribution of a bias-corrected sum-of-squares and a max-type statistic for fixed T, N -> infinity, strong single-factor errors; show the Pesaran-CD style correction fails for fixed T (incidental-parameters-type bias) and give a factor-robust (cross-sectionally demeaned across g within donor) version with exact size under Gaussian errors; power vs sparse alternatives.
problems.data_test: Leave-donor-out ridge predictions for 6 tasks x 3 encoders: gene-wise calibration slope/intercept per donor; semi-synthetic nulls by resampling donor residual vectors to check size, real labels for power. The depth factor (0.650 of CCRCC between-donor variance) is exactly the strong common factor.
problems.scoop_check: 4 queries (web_search x2, arXiv API x2 returned physics junk). Found no N>T joint MZ test. Nearby: Fosten-Gutknecht arXiv:2302.02747 (multivariate quantile MZ, G=4 series), Qu-Timmermann-Zhu cross-sectional comparison tests (rady.ucsd.edu), a paper on the incidental-parameters bias of the CD test (doi 10.1080/07350015.2021.1906687, authors not retrieved), Massacci et al. arXiv:2507.17599 randomised alpha test. Risk: Pesaran-Yamagata-type quadratic or max statistics for SUR with equation-specific regressors may already cover it; the digest holds Shift G (finite-K calibration-slope t-test) and Multi J (Clark-West) that overlap in spirit.
problems.finance_transfer: Multi-asset forecast-rationality testing with N>T (analyst forecasts, ML return forecasts across assets) where a common market factor contaminates all errors.

problems.title: SNR frontier of random-feature ridge when signal strength varies randomly across groups (donors/periods) and the penalty is chosen by leave-group-out CV
problems.source_and_stated_gap: 'Is sophistication a panacea? The learning capacity of random feature models for financial forecasting' (arXiv:2610.27255, Oct 2026; authors not extracted). Sec on posterior drift: the SNR needed to beat the zero forecast is higher under drift w (fixed, e.g. w=0.7); the authors leave the conjectured universality of the SNR frontier across eigenfunction distributions open, and note tighter bounds are possible.
problems.formulation: Groups d=1..G with group-specific SNR rho_d ~ Pi (random), training groups and a new test group; ridge/RF-ridge with penalty lambda. Define the frontier set {(rho, lambda): risk < zero-forecast risk} for the mixture and the minimum penalty that guards against the worst plausible test-group SNR.
problems.formal_result_aim: Deterministic-equivalent risk under random group SNR; closed form for the minimum safe penalty as a functional of Pi; proof that leave-group-out CV with G groups consistently estimates the frontier with sqrt(G) error; universality remark.
problems.data_test: Per-donor within-donor prediction-label correlation (reported 0.11-0.20 Visium, 0.52-0.63 Xenium) gives an empirical Pi; check whether leave-donor-out risk of unpenalised vs tuned ridge matches the predicted frontier, and why donor-level prediction does not beat a constant for the median Visium gene.
problems.scoop_check: 4 queries (web_search x2, arXiv API x2). The base frontier with a fixed drift parameter is in 2610.27255 itself. Optimal ridge under covariate shift: arXiv:2404.01233 (Optimal Ridge Regularization for Out-of-Distribution Prediction; authors not retrieved). Ridge with correlated samples and CV: Atanasov et al. arXiv:2408.04607 (already in the digest as the closest to Repr A/I). Feature-group ridge: sigma-Ridge arXiv:2010.15817 (groups of features, not of samples). I did not find random per-group SNR; but the digest Shift F and Repr A/I cover neighbouring ground, so overlap risk is high.
problems.finance_transfer: Choosing a minimum penalty for ML return forecasts when predictability is regime-dependent (random SNR across periods).

problems.title: Latent-regressor / generated-regressor correction when the measurement errors of several ML predictions share a common component and no validation labels exist
problems.source_and_stated_gap: Canen and Enamorado, 'When Predictions Become Regressors' (arXiv:2608.02909, Aug 2026), limitation paragraph and Conclusion: the split-sample correction assumes errors uncorrelated across observations conditional on the input; correlations induced by unobservables are plausible; future work on more than two splits or multiple prediction models, nonlinear outcome models and more complex dependence. Also Battaglia et al. (arXiv:2402.15585): errors can be nonclassical, difficult to correct.
problems.formulation: Downstream regression z_i = beta*theta_i + c_i, theta_i latent, K measurements w_ik = theta_i + u_ik with u_ik = s_i + v_ik, s_i a common component (ten encoders reading the same image), no labelled theta. Identify or bound beta.
problems.formal_result_aim: Partial-identification bounds for beta under a one-factor error structure with sign restrictions; a consistent estimator when K >= 3 and the common component is orthogonal to a known covariate block; asymptotic variance.
problems.data_test: Use spot-level labels as the 'latent' truth: regress an observed downstream outcome (e.g. a second gene or nuclear morphology summary) on the ten encoder predictions of expression, apply the correction without labels, compare with the labelled benchmark. Finance/social-science analyses cannot do this because truth is unobserved.
problems.scoop_check: 3 queries (web_search x1, arXiv API x2 junk). Split-indicator correction with independent errors: Jerzak et al. arXiv:2507.22218; ML-generated regressor inference: arXiv:2402.15585, arXiv:2608.02909, arXiv:2301.10643; errors-in-variables with multiple indicators is classical (Schennach-type identification, not retrieved here). The digest already holds triple-collocation items (Repr H, Shift D) and the PPI exclusion is adjacent. High overlap risk.
problems.finance_transfer: Text- and LLM-generated signals used as regressors in asset-pricing regressions with correlated embedding errors.

problems.title: Inference on forecaster alignment / IC with few periods (donors) and spatially dependent units within a period
problems.source_and_stated_gap: Soleimani, 'Target alignment, dilution and forecast selection...' (arXiv:2609.26303, Sep 2026), Limitations bullets and results: bootstrap inference for the joint alignment test is oversized under the dependence in the first panel; a single horizon, six outer origins, procedures tuned on the evaluation data. Ding-Sun 2023 supplies IC asymptotics for large T.
problems.formulation: Dates d=1..G (G=15-25), units j=1..n_d with spatial dependence, K forecasters; alignment a_dk = corr_j(forecast, target); test H0: max_k mean_d a_dk <= 0 and the marginal gain of adding forecaster K+1 (improvement vs dilution).
problems.formal_result_aim: Finite-G valid test combining Clifford-Richardson-type within-date effective-n correction with an across-date sign-flip or t_{G-1} reference; size under heterogeneous per-date n_d and alignment variances.
problems.data_test: Per-donor Pearson correlations of 10 encoders on 6 tasks (rank-one skill across encoders gives dilution by construction); size checked by permuting spot labels within donors preserving spatial blocks.
problems.scoop_check: 4 queries (web_search x2, arXiv API x2 junk). Within-date spatial correction exists since 1989 (Clifford-Richardson-Hemon, PubMed 2720048; Dutilleul 1993); IC asymptotics: Ding-Sun 2023 (J. Asset Management); small-T cross-sectional accuracy tests: Qu-Timmermann-Zhu; the digest BENCH (mostly_taken), Forecast F/H, Multi E and the SIGN item cover the across-donor part. Essentially a recombination of published pieces.
